newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Southcorp strike stops fridge output-union.
newsitem.headline: Southcorp strike stops fridge output-union.

text.p: A strike by more than 200 workers at Southcorp Holding Ltd's refrigeration plant in Melbourne had stopped production at the plant, causing short supplies of some models, the Australian Manufacturing Workers' Union (AMWU) said on Monday.

AMWU organiser Judith Klepner told Reuters picket lines had been set up outside the plant in the suburb of Clayton and the strike, which involved production, stores, maintenance, technical, supervisory and cleaning staff, had "all but" closed the plant.
About four refrigerator models were in short supply and the strike had also affected the replacement of fridge doors which had been recalled, she said.
Southcorp Appliances management could not be contacted for comment.

Klepner said the workers, members of the AMWU, Australian Services Union (ASU), Australian Workers Union (AWU), Electrical Trades Union (ETU) and the National Union of Workers (NUW), went on strike last Tuesday, after protracted negotiations with Southcorp Appliances on a collective work agreement.

Workers, seeking a negotiable 15 percent wage rise a year, had rejected a two percent offer as "substandard" given Reserve Bank figures which showed the average increase in manufacturing agreements at more than five percent, she said.
They were also concerned at Southcorp's moves for wage rises linked to productivity improvements which were based on uncertain outcomes and on factors outside the control of employees, she said.

Klepner said the unions were happy to meet with management at any time it wished to speak constructively, but the strike had been called indefinitely and workers were determined to persist until they had a fair deal.
